correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the Dirichlet directing vector makes adjacent observations iid categorical, so each change indicator has conditional mean equal to latent Gini–Simpson diversity. Dirichlet fourth moments give the diversity variance; adjacent and disjoint edge-pair moments give the complete variance of the transition count. The algebra was independently checked by exact rational enumeration over 20,007 sequence states. No finite computation is used as a substitute for the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Adjacent changes are a canonical local sequence observable, while Gini–Simpson diversity is a canonical latent concentration functional. The theorem gives an exact finite-sample bridge between them under reinforcement, quantifies the amount of latent diversity information captured by order-local transitions, and shows asymptotically perfect correlation with an explicit first-order rate. This is a structural relation rather than a recomputation of a marginal run distribution.
